claim: The audit configuration named 'demo-basic-config' in the 'default' workspace can be retrieved using either the NeMoPlatform Python client or the nmpauditconfigsget CLI command.
premises: The Python code imports os and NeMoPlatform, initializes a client with base_url and workspace, then retrieves the config by name and workspace.
The CLI command 'nmpauditconfigsget demo-basic-config --workspace default -f json' is shown as an alternative method.
Both methods produce JSON output representing the same audit configuration.

claim: If you receive a 401 Unauthorized error on every request, authentication is enabled but no valid credentials are being sent.
premises: Auth is enabled but no valid credentials are being sent.
Check if auth is enabled: curl ${ BASE_URL } /apis/auth/discovery If auth_enabled is true , all requests must include credentials.
Check your token status: nmp auth status The CLI and SDK automatically refresh expired tokens. If automatic refresh fails (e.g., the refresh token itself has expired), re-login: nmp auth login

claim: A 403 Forbidden error occurs when authentication succeeds but authorization fails due to insufficient role or missing token scopes.
premises: Authentication succeeded, but authorization failed — the user lacks the required role or the token lacks the required scope.
Check your role binding in the workspace: nmp members list --workspace <workspace-name> Verify your email appears and has the expected role (Viewer, Editor, or Admin).

Check your token scopes. Decode the JWT and verify the required scopes are present: nmp auth token | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d 2 >/dev/null | python -m json.tool Look for scp or scope — ensure platform:write is present for write operations.

claim: The nmp auth login command fails with an IdP error when the requested scope is not configured or admin consent has not been granted in Azure AD.
premises: The requested scope is not configured or admin consent has not been granted.
Fix : In Azure Portal → App Registration → API Permissions, ensure: Custom scopes ( platform:read , platform:write ) are defined under “Expose an API”
Admin consent is granted for the scopes

claim: Device flow authentication fails if the Identity Provider does not have public client flows enabled for the NMP application.
premises: Your IdP doesn’t have device flow enabled for the NMP application.
Azure AD : App Registration → Authentication → “Allow public client flows” → Yes
Okta : Application → General → “Device Authorization” grant type must be enabled

claim: Authentication fails due to a client ID mismatch between NMP configuration and the Identity Provider application.
premises: The client_id in NMP config doesn’t match the application in your IdP.
Fix : Verify auth.oidc.client_id matches the client ID in your IdP exactly.

claim: A workspace cannot be deleted if it contains resources or if the user lacks the Admin role.
premises: Cause : The workspace contains resources, or you don’t have the Admin role.
Check the error message — it lists which entity types exist: { "detail" : "Cannot delete workspace 'ml-team': workspace contains entities that must be deleted first: project (3), dataset (5)" }
Delete all resources in the workspace first, then retry.

claim: Gateway-level authentication fails if the gateway does not properly set or strip authentication headers.
premises: Cause : Headers are not being set or stripped correctly by the gateway.
Check that X-NMP-Authorized: true is being set by the gateway on allowed requests. If services don’t see this header, they fall through to their own PDP call.
Check that auth headers are stripped from external requests. Try sending a request with X-NMP-Authorized: true from outside the cluster — it should be stripped by the gateway.

claim: Role changes do not take effect immediately due to policy data propagation delay in the PDP cache.
premises: Cause : Policy data propagation delay.
The PDP caches role binding data. After adding or removing a member: Embedded PDP : Wait up to policy_data_refresh_interval seconds (default: 30).
External OPA : Wait up to 2 × bundle_cache_seconds (default: ~10 seconds).

claim: A PlatformAdmin cannot access a workspace if the principal identity in the token does not exactly match the admin_email configured in the system.
premises: Cause : The principal identity doesn’t match admin_email exactly.
Check the admin_email in your config — it’s case-sensitive.
Verify the email in your token matches. Decode the JWT and check the email/upn claim.

claim: The quickstart.prompts module provides interactive functions for configuration and registry authentication detection.
premises: The module contains functions: detect_registry_auth_type, prompt_for_configuration, and prompt_for_registry_credentials.
These functions are described as detecting registry auth type, providing an interactive configuration wizard, and prompting for registry credentials after a pull failure.
The module is titled 'Interactive prompts for quickstart configuration.'
